dig up verb

find out (facts)

also dig up something about, unearth, ferret out

classical

Cic. Att. 13.30.2 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 96

ēruō, ēruere, ēruī, ērutum

verb, third conjugation

dig up, ferret out (facts)

Literally “to dig out”. Traupman has quicquam ēruere dē (+ abl.); but quicquam belongs in negative sentences and questions, so in a plain statement aliquid ēruere dē ….

Examples

  • mī sīcundē potes, ēruēs, quī decem lēgātī Mummiō fuerint

    dig up for me, if you can from anywhere, who the ten commissioners with Mummius wereCic. Att. 13.30.2 (Lewis & Short)

SourcesLewis & Short: eruo

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 96, checked against the searchable text and the page images of the book.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
